page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor. It features 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz, with a single thread per core configuration. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core.

A defining characteristic of this instance is its massive local storage capacity, which consists of 47,244 GB of HDD storage. This high-density local storage is bundled directly with the instance. For external connectivity, the server provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.d1.4xlarge is its reliance on HDD storage rather than SSDs, which prioritizes raw storage capacity and cost-effective bulk data retention over high random IOPS. The absence of hyperthreading means each of the 16 vCPUs maps to a dedicated physical core, ensuring consistent compute performance. This hardware profile is designed for storage-intensive workloads such as large-scale data warehousing, log processing, and big data analytics that require massive local storage capacity.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.4xlarge is an x86_64 server instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 16 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The most prominent feature of this instance is its bundled 47,244 GB of local HDD storage, designed for high-capacity data retention. Networking capabilities include a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, the instance lacks hyperthreading, which guarantees dedicated physical execution resources per vCPU. This configuration presents a clear tradeoff, offering massive storage volume at the expense of the faster random access speeds associated with SSDs. It is structured for storage-heavy workloads, including distributed file systems, big data processing, and large-scale log archiving.
